data.title: ‘Just look at this monstrosity!’ Inside Britain’s bilious back yard shed wars
data.description: The number of luxury sheds and garden rooms has rocketed since the pandemic – fuelled by those wanting an office, a gym or extra living space. Meanwhile, the resentment between neighbours has been rising, too Linda loves her shed. She loves that she can work there rather than in her dining room, which her toddler likes to tear through. She loves its Scandinavian vibe – it’s clad in wood and set on decking at the bottom of her garden. She loves the views of the countryside from the window by her desk. Or she did. Her desk faces the wall now, because she’s too nervous to face her neighbour. She never sits on the decking, either. “What if they see me?” she says. “It’s a horrible feeling.” Linda’s neighbours are unhappy about her shed, or “garden room”, which is actually two rooms. They do not like its size (7.25 metres by 2.74 metres, or 3.5 metres if you include the raised decking) or its position, about 30 metres away from their house. Linda says they have barely spoken since the construction, which is awkward, as the gardens are separated by a low fence. Continue reading...

data.title: A leftwing victory in Berlin shows people want freedom, and liberals cannot deliver it | Eva von Redecker
data.description: Die Linke’s surge was propelled by a compelling promise: for voters to have the freedom to stay in their city. This is how to fight back against the far right The German leftwing party Die Linke won the state elections in Berlin on 20 September. It’s unclear whether the party will be able to form a coalition, appoint its lead candidate Elif Eralp as mayor , and follow through on her core campaign promise: to socialise the housing stock of the city’s biggest real-estate companies. A barrage of accusations started to circulate immediately after the results came in. Even by the standards of present-day polarisation, the pitch was extreme. On the basis of one leaked chat and one rapper’s performance , the party was described as schmoozing with criminal clans and endangering the lives of Berlin Jews . Accusations of antisemitism prompted the Greens and the SPD – potential coalition partners – to question any potential cooperation, while “alt-right” opinion-makers suggested that “Hamas and Hezbollah” had won the elections , or that the German Democratic Republic (the old East Germany) was about to come back. Alice Weidel of the rightwing AfD alleged that Die Linke intended to “shoot the rich”. Continue reading...

data.title: Saving the Siamese crocodile: Cambodia moves to protect one of the world’s last wild populations
data.description: Indigenous communities play crucial role, as ‘genetic bank’ area of wetland offers hope for critically endangered reptile In the 1990s, conservationists in Cambodia feared the Siamese crocodile had disappeared for good. Fishing and hunting had devastated the species throughout the 20th century, leaving populations across its native south-east Asia on the brink of extinction. But in villages dotted among the wetlands of the remote Cardamom mountains, Indigenous Chorng communities still reported seeing them. Passing this knowledge to researchers surveying the area in 2000 led to an official recording of the species – and bolstered the mission to revive the population. Continue reading...

data.title: As AI models go rogue, do you still trust OpenAI and Anthropic to stop them? I don’t and neither should you | Chris Stokel-Walker
data.description: The need for independent regulation grows more obvious by the day. We must keep this tech in check before it’s too late OpenAI scraps release of new model over safety concerns in internal testing Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. Fool me more than 16,000 times – as OpenAI agents did to a UN public data hub while repeatedly trying to find its way around the UN’s cyber-blocks – and perhaps it’s time to admit the system we have for keeping AI agents under control isn’t working particularly well. The news about AI systems cropping up in places they shouldn’t sounds alarming. Though the description of these as “hacks” is perhaps overstating things, AI has exploited issues in IT systems that humans simply haven’t got around to finding. It’s also important to note that we shouldn’t be worried that the machines have suddenly become sentient and decided to rebel against humanity . There is not enough evidence to suggest that’s what is happening. The systems are simply following instructions and trying to complete the tasks they have been given, even if they’re sometimes finding unintended ways around obstacles to do so. Chris Stokel-Walker is the author of TikTok Boom: The Inside Story of the World’s Favourite App Continue reading...

data.title: The Pussy Riot activist turned Kremlin informer – podcast
data.description: Their opposition to Putin led to two of the group being sent to brutal prison camps. Then another was found to be spying for the Kremlin. Shaun Walker reports It’s January 2012 and Pussy Riot are filming a video in Red Square, Moscow. As snow covers the cobbles and dusts the onion globes of St Basil’s Cathedral, the clock on the Kremlin chimes 11am. Eight women in colourful balaclavas leap on to a stone platform, one with an electric guitar. They start playing their latest song, Putin Has Chickened Out. It’s pretty punchy, with lyrics such as: “The rebellious column is heading to the Kremlin / Windows are exploding in FSB offices.” The group had formed a few months earlier after Vladimir Putin announced that he planned to return to the Kremlin for a third term as president. Inspired by the Arab spring the previous year, they hoped to bring revolution to Russia and stop Putin. Instead, the state cracked down hard. Three Pussy Riot members were found guilty of hooliganism after later protests, with two spending two years in some of Russia’s harshest jails. Continue reading...

data.title: Large shark stuck in South Korean city canal draws 600,000 visitors
data.description: Port city of Busan inundated with tourists keen to see the 3.5-metre animal close up A large shark has become an unlikely tourist attraction after getting trapped in a narrow city canal in South Korea for more than a week. More than 600,000 people are estimated to have visited a waterfront park in the southern port city of Busan since the 3.5-metre shark – nicknamed Bukang-i after the name of Busan’s North Port – was first spotted in its waterway on 18 September. data.title: Why is Israel so afraid of the film NAZA? We spoke to its directors – Stateside with Kai and Carter
data.description: When NAZA premiered at Venice earlier this month, it sent shockwaves across the globe. Composed of interviews with 24 anonymous Israeli intelligence officers and soldiers, NAZA is a haunting exposé of the tools that the Israeli military uses to carry out the remote killing of Palestinians in Gaza – including AI, mass surveillance, and devastating airstrikes that kill civilians and raze homes. Now, the Israeli government is treating NAZA like a national security crisis. Benjamin Netanyahu is even pushing for legislation that could strip the film's two directors of their Israeli citizenship. Host Carter Sherman speaks with the directors of NAZA, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, in one of their first interviews with an American journalist. The film, which was produced by the Guardian, will open in New York this week and soon expand to theaters worldwide. It will also stream, for free, on the Guardian website in November Read the reporting in NAZA originally published in the Guardian: ‘The Gospel’: how Israel uses AI to select bombing targets in Gaza Revealed: Israeli military creating ChatGPT-like tool using vast collection of Palestinian surveillance data Continue reading...

data.title: Murdered for their eyes: people with albinism living in terror in Madagascar
data.description: The country is struggling to address a rise in attacks, with a record 13 people – mostly children – killed this year for body parts, which some believe can bring good fortune Not long after midnight in late May this year, three men barged through the door of the small room where Nicole Soalala lived with her family on the outskirts of Toliara, a coastal city in the south of Madagascar. Her husband got up to ask what they wanted, but they attacked him with a piece of wood and an axe. Soalala, 32, grabbed her youngest child, Landricia – an 18-month-old girl with albinism – and hoisted her on to her back, holding her there with a piece of fabric she started to wrap around herself. Her eldest daughter, 15, hid under the table with her other two children, aged six and three. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Online sex workers literally have to bare it all’: why Patricia Nilsson is exposing the world’s biggest porn bosses
data.description: As a business journalist, Nilsson began rigorously reporting on the power players of the adult industry, who prefer to remain in the shadows. Along the way, she uncovered how porn has shaped the internet – and our lives as a whole There was a time, a few decades ago, when the men who owned the world’s biggest pornography businesses were happy to be famous. They paraded a lifestyle they hoped looked glamorous, appearing in public dressed in silk pyjamas or with a woman in swimwear on each arm. Porn moguls like Hustler’s Larry Flynt or Playboy’s Hugh Hefner were household names. “Say what you want about these old perverts, who once set the tone of our sexual culture, but at least you knew who they were and what they were selling,” Patricia Nilsson writes in her new book, Guilty Pleasure: The Pornification of the Internet, the Economy, and Everything Else. “These days, the men calling the shots are nowhere to be seen.” Continue reading...

data.title: No island of strangers: why I’m using art to unite a fractured nation
data.description: Fear of outsiders is the defining issue of our times. But is it actually our own selves we’re scared of? And could art hold the answers? Here, the British Art Show’s curator reveals why he’s exploring our deepest dreams and nightmares One of the moral low points of Keir Starmer’s tenure at Downing Street was his “island of strangers” speech, with its rhetorical echoes of Enoch Powell and dispiriting description of a nation fractured by difference. After widespread criticism, Starmer recanted his words, if not the sentiment behind them. Yet his choice of language was a reminder of how the idea of the stranger – representing immigration, but also wider, more inchoate anxieties about otherness and difference – holds such a potent place in Britain today. In fact, from masked anti-migrant protesters on the south coast to xenophobic riots over the summer, from politicians vowing to stop the boats to immigration polling as the No 1 concern among UK voters, it’s probably true to say that fear of the stranger is the totemic issue of our times. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A genre-defying monument’: how Sign o’ the Times captured Prince at his creative peak
data.description: As a new book on the Paisley Park polymath is released, author John McKie explains why Prince’s 1987 album is the ultimate showcase of his genius By the early 1980s, Prince had cemented his place as a pop heavyweight with the phenomenal success of his 1999 album, as well as becoming a movie star thanks to Purple Rain. Even when his second film, the old Hollywood throwback Under the Cherry Moon, bombed worldwide in 1986, he notched another massive hit off its soundtrack with Kiss. It didn’t matter if audiences didn’t understand; Prince kept moving forward. That restless spirit propelled Prince’s final masterpiece, 1987’s Sign o’ the Times, as he dabbled with different directions. Anything seemed on the table: maybe he would drop another album with his backing band, The Revolution, or he would explore his feminine alter-ego Camille with a self-titled album. He even, at one point, wanted to put out a triple album, a reasonable response to the vast collection of music that Prince was creating. “Sometimes when people are in a place of transition, they’re distracted,” said John McKie, whose new book Prince: A Sign o’ the Times follows the pop legend’s career through the lens of this classic. “For Prince, he focused on his music.” Continue reading...

data.title: Saunas, cinnamon buns and coastal scenery on the new rail route from Malmö to Oslo
data.description: A new direct train service connects the far south of Sweden to the Norwegian capital in just over six hours, with the option of stopping off in the seaside town of Varberg or lively Gothenburg en route ‘This carriage is due for modernisation. Don’t miss the opportunity to experience 90s Germany style,” reads the sign on the door to the dining carriage. The couple inside aren’t missing theirs: they’re taking endless selfies in the clinical pink-and-turquoise carriage that looks like a hospital canteen and smells like cinnamon buns and strong filter coffee. I’m on Snälltåget’s iconic red-shelled train, on the Swedish rail company’s new route from Malmö to Oslo – a 6.5-hour journey along Sweden’s picturesque western corridor. Until now, the journey between the two cities involved long bus rides and fragmented train transfers. This direct line is easier and cheaper, with tickets starting at £11 each way. It’s already a hit, shuttling more than 25,000 passengers since launching this summer. Continue reading...

data.title: On the rocks? Scotch distilleries pause production as unsold ‘whisky loch’ grows
data.description: Demand for Scotland’s most famous export has slumped, with industry facing job cuts and closures Obscured by the Scottish countryside on the outskirts of Kirkcaldy, Cluny bond is, in effect, a small town built to store whisky. By the time the latest set of warehouses are finished on the former opencast coal mine, Diageo’s 220-hectare (544-acre) maturation campus will be able to store almost 3m casks of Scotch. The drinks multinational needs the space. After a 15-year boom turbocharged by the Covid-19 pandemic, demand for Scotch whisky has slumped around the world. Distilleries have paused production across Scotland to avoid adding to the glut of supply, known as a “whisky loch” – the equivalent of a “wine lake”. Continue reading...

data.title: The Fall of the West by Owen Jones review – a bracing history of the changing world order
data.description: A journalist charts a quarter century of geopolitical hubris and economic overreach Like many Britons born in the 1980s, the journalist and Guardian columnist Owen Jones came of age with Tony Blair’s platitudes ringing in his ears. Politics at the turn of the millennium was a story of temporary dispensations mistaken for eternal truths: the definitive triumph of free market ideology; US military supremacy; a rules-based global order. As Jones recounts in his new book, these certainties would come crashing down over the next quarter of a century amid a succession of economic failures, foreign policy disasters and political crises. Indeed, “the west” itself – as a shorthand for the US plus the wealthier western European nations – feels almost quaint today, given the increasing unilateralism of the administration in Washington. But in the 2000s it was part of the lexicon, as if the hemisphere were a political actor in its own right. Revisiting the US-led wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, we are reminded not just of their horrific death tolls (totalling half a million, by conservative estimates) but also their total strategic failure; the 2021 evacuation of Kabul airport, Jones writes, was “among the starkest images of American decline yet broadcast to the world”. Continue reading...

data.title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
data.description: Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere. The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. data.title: Why am I obsessed with China’s ancient golden age? I took my daughter on a trip to find out
data.description: I felt a duty to write about the Tang dynasty and its incredible social and cultural sophistication – but also to connect my Chinese past with my child During the Tang dynasty , which lasted from the seventh to the early 10th century, Vikings were raiding the coasts of what today is called Europe. In the small archipelago now known as Britain, Anglo-Saxon kingdoms flitted by. Meanwhile, in Mesoamerica, after 3,000 years of flourishing, the Maya civilisation was collapsing . In the east, China had been united for nine centuries and the Tang dynasty was already a proverbial high point of world culture. Continue reading...

data.title: How Senate Democrats can stop Trump from stealing the midterms | David Walbert
data.description: Republicans could lean on congressional procedure to defy the will of voters. But if they try that, the Senate has a clear way to fight back Having lost his mail-in ballot case , Donald Trump will likely resort to ever more extreme ways to try to hold a Republican Congress in November’s elections. His last-ditch effort to count Joe Biden out in 2020 was for Republicans to “investigate” states Biden narrowly won; proclaim fabricated allegations of “stolen elections” to be true; and then reassign those states’ electoral votes to Trump. I have previously described how that same playbook could be used to try to steal the midterms if a Democratic margin of victory in the House is relatively narrow. Continue reading...

data.title: Cutting immigration to the UK means billions less for the Treasury. Can the country really afford that? | Zoe Williams
data.description: ‘Taking back control’ turns out to be staggeringly expensive. That’s something to mull over as budget day approaches Every 100,000 immigrants lost to the UK costs the treasury £7bn , according to the Office for Budget Responsibility. That figure is unsurprising if you’ve been concentrating at all – the calculation was made in 2024 – but at the same time completely staggering. Nobody ever says, “The chancellor’s going to be in trouble because of all those lost immigrants”; few people remark on, let alone decry, the very large numbers of migrants who have been lost due to policy decisions. And then, as budget day approaches, brute facts and mathematical realities assert themselves: migration numbers have been falling faster than anticipated. And if you take all the measures you can to discourage international students, skilled workers, all imaginable young, mobile people who work and don’t get ill, while at the same time preventing with all your might any legitimate employment opportunities for asylum seekers, you will suffer a hit to the national coffers. Continue reading...

data.title: Britons are not ageing healthily – we need to learn from countries that have made it a priority | Devi Sridhar
data.description: Although we’re living longer, the data on healthy life expectancy in the UK isn’t good. Andy Burnham must reverse this trend to protect the NHS and social care Prof Devi Sridhar is chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh, and the author of How Not to Die (Too Soon) The prime minister has put forward his bold proposal for a universal, NHS-style social care service. In doing so, Andy Burnham has put the spotlight back on one of the major challenges facing almost everywhere in the world: how to manage the demographic changes linked to an ageing society. It’s an important discussion. But what if government didn’t just look at how to care for people in their later years and instead spent real political capital on policies to help people live longer independently, and in good health? The data isn’t pretty on this. While the trend over the past half-century in almost all countries has been for people to live longer, healthy life expectancy has been consistently falling. Prof Devi Sridhar is chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh, and the author of How Not to Die (Too Soon) Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the Drumcree parade: ghosts from the past have brought Stormont to the brink | Editorial
data.description: A reckless decision to authorise an Orange Order parade with a notorious history has deepened the political crisis in the Northern Ireland executive The last time that the Orange Order successfully marched from Drumcree parish church down the Garvaghy Road, a mainly Catholic part of Portadown, it required a British army presence and a lockdown of locals forced off their own streets. The 1997 parade was preceded by loyalist death threats and followed by nationalist riots, in which more than 160 people were injured. The lengthy track record of lethal violence and disorder associated with the march led the Parades Commission – established the following year as part of the peace process – to ban it. On Sunday, however, in scenes that rolled back the years in deeply unwelcome fashion, the old traumas and hostilities were recklessly allowed to resurface. Unfathomably, after a routine decision to renew the ban this year was challenged on procedural grounds, the commissioners reversed their ruling late last week and permitted a march to go ahead on a limited scale. The entirely predictable result was a tense standoff and a political crisis in Stormont, after protesters blocked the Garvaghy Road route until the early hours of Monday morning. data.translatedDescription: A reckless decision to authorise an Orange Order parade with a notorious history has deepened the political crisis in the Northern Ireland executive The last time that the Orange Order successfully marched from Drumcree parish church down the Garvaghy Road, a mainly Catholic part of Portadown, it required a British army presence and a lockdown of locals forced off their own streets. The 1997 parade was preceded by loyalist death threats and followed by nationalist riots, in which more than 160 people were injured. The lengthy track record of lethal violence and disorder associated with the march led the Parades Commission – established the following year as part of the peace process – to ban it. On Sunday, however, in scenes that rolled back the years in deeply unwelcome fashion, the old traumas and hostilities were recklessly allowed to resurface. Unfathomably, after a routine decision to renew the ban this year was challenged on procedural grounds, the commissioners reversed their ruling late last week and permitted a march to go ahead on a limited scale. The entirely predictable result was a tense standoff and a political crisis in Stormont, after protesters blocked the Garvaghy Road route until the early hours of Monday morning. data.title: American exodus: why do so many US NHL stars want out of Canada?
data.description: Players across the league are leaving their teams up north to return home. It’s prompted questions around money, tax rates, geopolitics and respect Back in September 1925, Frederick Wilson, sports editor at the Globe, explained the fear among hockey fans that Canadian teams might not be able to compete for players against the new US teams like New York or Boston that were entering the pro league. “Will it be a matter of money?” Wilson headlined his piece. And for about a century, money was the recurrent nexus of the Canadian hockey panic, proven by franchise departures and depleted buying power. At the time, Wilson reassured everyone that, no matter the big US cash, everyone on the ice would be Canadian anyway. “It will be some years before the [US] will be in a position to furnish players,” he wrote. He was right about that. It took a long time for the US to catch up to Canada in on-ice talent. But now that it has, should we expect Americans to want to play anywhere else than the US? For 100 years Canada has worried that the US would just buy all the best hockey players. But now it makes its own and, as the new NHL season gets underway on Tuesday night, they want to go home. Continue reading...

data.title: Paris magic and tradition keep the Arc in a class of its own above the latest gimmicks
data.description: It may not be the official best race in the world but winning at Longchamp still confers a status little else can match When France-Galop announced in June that geldings will be allowed to run in the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe from 2027, there was an underlying sense that action was needed to maintain the race’s status as Europe’s showpiece event. The Arc was officially the World’s Best Horse Race in five of the seven years after the award was introduced in 2015, but has fallen short of rivals including the Japan Cup and the Breeders’ Cup Classic since 2021 at a time when several geldings, including the French-trained Calandagan, have been among the world’s top-rated middle-distance horses. Yet even a brief glance through the leading contenders for this year’s race at Longchamp on Sunday offers reminders that the Arc has a heritage and mystique that will always set it apart among the championship events around the globe. The names of the winners, both equine and human, retain their currency from one generation to the next. Continue reading...

data.title: Three deaths, three states, 24 hours: one day in ICE’s quiet but ‘gruesome’ surge
data.description: These men in Maine, Georgia and Florida shared no ties – until they became casualties in the latest phase of Trump’s anti-immigration campaign Gone in 90 seconds: an ‘invisibilized’ ICE is arresting more people than ever It was 7am on 13 July this year. A warm, sunny morning, as residents of Biddeford, Maine , left their homes, got into their cars and began their commute. Joan Sebastián Durán Guerrero came out of the apartment he lived in with his partner and daughter and drove off in his white car. Minutes later, neighbors heard three pops. Durán Guerrero was dead . More than 1,200 miles (1,900km) away in Ocilla, Georgia , Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva was shuffled on to a bus. Private sector guards and Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) officials were beginning the process of transferring him and several other immigrants from one detention center to another nearly two hours away. Ten minutes into the ride, he became unconscious. Doctors at a nearby hospital pronounced him dead . Continue reading...

data.title: Investigation of alleged gang-rape at Cornell University fraternity house reopened

According to lawyers for the student, who filed a civil lawsuit against the university and her alleged attackers earlier in September, only two members of the Chi Phi fraternity were expelled after the October 2024 incident, in which she said she was drugged and repeatedly raped over the course of seven hours. Information and support for anyone affected by rape or sexual abuse issues is available from the following organizations. In the US, Rainn offers support on 800-656-4673. data.title: Child review – jump scares abound in twisty organ transplant fable that keeps horror at its heart
data.description: This Luxembourg-made movie about a couple who venture east to save their son features some impressive film-making Stippled with first-world guilt about income inequality even between fellow EU member states, this Luxembourg-made horror sprinkles a bit of liberal fairy dust over what is otherwise a pretty straight-up, if twisty, horror setup: a grunting, inarticulate and physically disfigured big baddie stalks the normie protagonists who shouldn’t have come round these impoverished parts. Think Grand Duchy Chainsaw Massacre, though admittedly without any chainsaws. There are sullen locals, a dilapidated farmhouse full of ominous clutter, ill intentions and horrible maiming. The unlucky visitors here are former couple Greg (Malik Zidi) and Anne (Brigitte Urhausen), who are co-parenting little Leo (Leo Todesco), a pre-adolescent who is lying in a hospital bed while waiting for a crucial organ transplant. A little time has to elapse before we learn that control-freak Anne blames likable doctor Greg for Leo’s condition because he took his eyes off the kid for just long enough for him to get hit by a car. But Greg is trying to make it up to her by accompanying his ex on a trip to an unnamed eastern European country (where folks speak Bulgarian) to acquire the organ Leo needs on the black market, their glide path lubricated with lots of cash and pre-arranged bribes to border guards and the like. Continue reading...

data.title: The Portuguese House review – picturesque, polite drama of secrets and revelations at a country estate
data.description: Spanish drama about people leaving their old lives behind plays out like a literary novel, with Manolo Solo excellent as a discombobulated gardener Out of the blue, a woman walks out on her husband. Bags packed and ready to go, at the last moment she crumples up the letter she has written to him and vanishes from their Madrid flat. So begins this drama featuring not one but three characters disappearing without a trace from their lives; it sounds soap opera-ish, but mostly The Portuguese House unfolds as polite elegant drama, told with such rich novelistic detail it often feels like it’s getting into the minds of the characters. Manolo Solo gives an excellent performance as the left-behind husband, Fernando, an introspective mild-mannered geography professor. After his wife’s disappearance, Fernando goes on holiday to Portugal, where he meets a gardener called Manuel. When Manuel drops dead of a heart attack, Fernando decides – like his wife – to leave his old life behind; he assumes Manuel’s identity and takes a job as the gardener at a Portuguese country estate. The owner, Amália (Maria de Medeiros), senses that this intellectual man with glasses and a clumsy way with the loppers is not the man she hired, but doesn’t push it – possibly because she is attracted to him. Continue reading...

data.title: April X review – Connor Storrie searches for missing twin in dystopian dream-tech sci-fi thriller
data.description: The star of Heated Rivalry does his best in this in this human-trafficking yarn, which gets progressively ickier and more exploitative Sketchy in every sense of the word, this sci-fi thriller is set in the not-too-distant future in a dystopian concrete city (actually mostly Bucharest looking like itself), where life is cheap but screenwriting conceits are clearly expensive, given most of the main ones here appear to be borrowed from other movies. Brother-and-sister twins Baxter ( Connor Storrie , from Heated Rivalry ) and April (Lilly Krug) are struggling to get by and mooching around the fringes of the criminal world, doing jobs on a spectrum of legality, though nothing especially harmful to themselves or others. He does petty crimes and she makes wigs and sells downloads of her own uncannily clear dreams (a nod to neglected 90s classics Strange Days and Until the End of the World where dream tech played key roles). Unfortunately, Baxter and his screw-up associate Ronny (Tourialay Akbari) fall into debt to and afoul with local kingpin Klein (Serban Pavlu), whose persistent use of Yiddish phrases and general parsimoniousness sets up the characterisation just on the edge of antisemitism. When Baxter cleans out his and April’s joint accounts and still comes up short, someone takes April and her archive of recorded dreams/memories. Suddenly, the action jumps ahead five years in the future and April is both still missing and yet, at a local brothel, all too ubiquitous where it seems she’s been cloned to make numerous sex workers. Continue reading...

data.description: ‘The day Saff came into the studio with red hair, I said, “We’re gonna be massive!” It was the missing link’ We always had a vision of mixing acid house with indie rock, and we managed to rent a space and build our own studio in London’s Shoreditch area, long before it got trendy. data.title: Stations by Louise Kennedy review – a superb follow-up to Trespasses
data.description: This tale of broken hearts and broken people moves from the Troubles of 70s Northern Ireland to an unforgiving London of squats and payphones Louise Kennedy’s first novel, Trespasses , was one of those rare triumphs, a debut that was not only rapturously received by critics but adored by readers around the world. A story of forbidden love set during the Troubles in 1970s Belfast, it was an international bestseller, translated into more than 20 languages. It was shortlisted for the 2023 Women’s prize and scooped debut fiction of the year at the British Book awards. A four-part television adaptation with Gillian Anderson aired last autumn on Channel 4. Inevitably Kennedy found herself lauded as an overnight success – much was made of her 30-year career as a professional chef – but in fact she had been writing short stories for a decade and to considerable acclaim; her first collection, The End of the World Is a Cul de Sac, was published in 2021. Included in that book was Belladonna, the story of Róisín, a young girl from Belfast who moves south with her mother and, ostracised by her new classmates, becomes friendly with the couple who live across the road. Like Briony Tallis in Ian McEwan’s Atonement, the prickly and precociously bright Róisín misinterprets the dynamic of her neighbours’ marriage to disastrous effect. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘You’ve got to be pretty tough to be a drag queen out there’: Damien Frost’s immaculate queer portraits
data.description: The photographer’s photos are so meticulously staged that viewers often assume they were taken in a studio – not behind a London nightclub or in an Australian goat field One bright spring day, the photographer Damien Frost arrived at a farm in Gungal, outside Muswellbrook, New South Wales. Goats grazed in a paddock, eucalyptus trees stretched into the brilliant blue sky and a tin shed weathered in the sun. Frost walked into the shed and entered another world. “It’s a drag studio,” says Frost. Lining the walls were dozens of wigs and rails of flamboyant outfits belonging to Beverly Fabulosity. “I’ve never seen anything like it. It was a very Priscilla scenario.” Frost grew up in Australia and is now based in London, where for more than a decade he has photographed drag queens and club kids for his acclaimed Night Flowers series. Since late August, he has been back in his home country, commissioned by Newcastle’s New Annual festival to photograph night owls in and around the city. These new portraits are being exhibited alongside a selection from Frost’s archive at Watt Space gallery as part of the festival. Continue reading...

data.title: Mighty Sparrow obituary
data.description: Trinidadian singer and songwriter hailed as a living legend and the greatest calypsonian of all time The singer and songwriter Mighty Sparrow, who has died aged 91, was quite simply the greatest calypsonian there has ever been. For at least five decades he was a monumental figure on the Caribbean music scene, while also capturing the hearts and minds of millions of fans around the world with self-penned songs that were the quintessential calypso mix of political commentary, humour, sexual innuendo and melody. Loved and feted by Trinidadians more than any other public figure in the island’s history, he was to calypso what Bob Marley was to reggae – an inspirational living legend. In Britain, no less than elsewhere, the sheer wit and quality of classic songs such as Jean and Dinah , Congo Man and Mae Mae brought calypso to many who would never otherwise have encountered the music form, particularly in the 1950s, 60s and 70s, when he was in his prime. Continue reading...

data.title: The pest I’ll never forget: I turned the toaster upside down. A mouse fell out
data.description: We tried humane traps, wire wool, hardcore cleaning regimes. Nothing worked. In the end, I wondered if the mice in our house were the real residents, while we were the intruders Some of the happiest years of my 20s were spent in a house-share in east London. Four of us were crammed into a three-bedroom terrace where the dining room had been turned into a bedroom. My housemates were my closest friends. We were young women with the kind of intense-bordering-on-codependent dynamic that becomes unsustainable later in life, when you have long-term partners, pets and children. We lived together, we went out together, in the summer we took our Argos tent to festivals together. We stayed up late discussing love-life and work dilemmas, often crowding round a phone to draft text messages. We were also not particularly clean, which meant our cluttered, chaotic house was the ideal home for mice. At first we told ourselves it was just one mouse we saw running along next to the skirting board or darting behind a sofa. But a quick scan of the internet confirmed our fears that it’s never just one – mice are social creatures, and they were likely in a nest-share similar to our house-share. A female mouse gives birth to a litter of five to eight mice and can be pregnant up to 10 times a year. We read forum posts that claimed mice were doubly incontinent (something I’ve since learned is fake news), and our horror began to grow. Continue reading...

data.title: Sanjana Modha’s quick and easy recipe for baked beans butter masala | Quick and easy
data.description: Transform two tins of baked beans into this creamy curry Masala baked beans, tadka baked beans, curried baked beans, spicy baked beans; all avatars of spice-laced baked beans are a mainstay of British Asian kitchens. We were raised on this stuff – use as a toastie filler, to smother jacket potatoes, or scoop them up with roti. Enter baked beans butter masala. With a sharp sweetness, a versatile tin of baked beans already has all the foundations required to build a brilliant butter masala, so all we’re doing is dressing them up. I like to think of it as though the beans are donning a frock made of all the good stuff: butter, cream and spices. This recipe is an edited extract from Modern Masala, by Sanjana Modha, published by Quadrille at £25. To order a copy for £22.50, go to guardianbookshop.com . Continue reading...

data.title: Houseplant hacks: should you water plants less in winter?
data.description: Don’t water based on the month or the season – be led by what the plant is actually doing The problem Cutting back on watering for winter has become so ingrained that people start rationing by the calendar, giving plants just a fraction of the water they had in summer, because the season changed. The hack The advice to reduce is because, as light levels drop, most houseplants slow their growth, use less water and dry out more slowly, so watering as you did in summer risks waterlogging the roots and causing rot. data.title: Concern mounts over slow-moving, planetary-scale ‘Kelvin’ wave heading for California
data.description: The ocean phenomenon could raise sea levels by up to a foot as El Niño keeps warm water trapped along the coast Concerns are mounting about an ocean phenomenon known as a Kelvin wave that could raise sea levels along the California coastline by up to a foot, as scientists say El Niño is supercharging the threat of storm surges and flooding in the coming months. As an incredibly strong El Niño continues to develop in the Pacific, the phenomenon brings with it a strange shift in the ocean. The Kelvin wave phenomenon is created when trade winds that usually blow from South America towards Asia die down or reverse in El Niño years, setting off a massive, slow-moving slosh of water. data.description: Older men and younger women were once an unremarkable screen pairing. One, they were peerless and two, this is the condition of middle age, constantly looking at the world thinking: “This could be considerably improved by the presence of Emma Thompson.” The notable casting update was Col Brandon, whose passion for Marianne would now be known as an “age gap” relationship. In the last film, Alan Rickman (born 1946) was in love with Winslet (born 1975), who cycles through a fair amount of: “Yuck, no thanks,” before having an epiphany. Continue reading...

data.title: Campaigners welcome Miliband’s claim Palestine Action ban not meant to criminalise ‘grannies’ – UK politics live
data.description: Defend Our Juries welcomes ‘honesty’ from foreign secretary and says his remarks will help in its legal challenge Burnham promises to roll back privatisation with government-backed grid plan Angela Rayner , the housing secretary, has apparently confirmed that Andy Burnham will float the prospect of getting rid of the pensions triple lock to help fund the creation of an NHS-style care service. Asked about the prospect on Sky’s Electoral Dysfunction podcast, Rayner said that Burnham was “absolutely right to start the conversation” and that he was being “brave”. The high principle on this is that people have paid in all their lives. They are willing, I think, to look at that. What they don’t want is what they consider to be, quite frankly, incompetent politicians that are going to take something from us to fill a black hole. When we met with Andy [Burnham] this week, it certainly wasn’t mentioned. But I do think that it’s important that Labour make sure that working-class people know that they’re on their side, and this would be a direction of travel that would say the opposite to that. What I understood the national care service to be was a universal benefit: everybody paid in and everybody gets out, and that is what actually the principle of that is. Going to a group of people who are getting around £12,500 a year in order to pay for it to take away their security is wrong. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Putin orders army expansion as Zelenskyy says more North Koreans to be deployed in Russia
data.description: Putin’s order comes as both Russian and Ukrainian forces suffer mounting casualties. What we know on day 1,679 Russian president Vladimir Putin has ordered ⁠an increase ​in the size ⁠of the army to 1.55 ⁠million ​active ‌servicemen , according ‌to a ‌presidential decree on Monday. The order comes as both Russia and Ukraine suffer mounting casualties in the more than four-and-a-half-year Ukraine war. The expansion, which follows a similar increase ordered in August, ‌will put the size ​of Russia’s armed forces at ⁠2,441,630. Of those are 1,550,000 ​active ​servicemen, an increase of ​15,500. Ukrainian president ⁠Volodymyr Zelenskyy said ​on X ​on ‌Monday ‌there were now more than 8,000 ‌North Korean ​troops on ⁠Russian territory ​and preparations ​were ​under way ​to ‌deploy ​another ​10,000 troops . Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un confirmed for the first time last year that North Korea had sent troops to fight for Russia in the war with Ukraine, with both leaders describing the soldiers as “heroes”. Citing “new data” on the deployment of North Korean troops to Russia, ⁠Zelenskyy said they were “being selected for training and subsequent deployment to Russia ”. North Korea has sent an estimated 14,000 to 15,000 ⁠troops to support Russia’s war in Ukraine since 2024, ​according to Ukrainian ​and South Korean estimates, ​with most deployed in the Kursk region to ​help repel a ‌Ukrainian incursion. Explosions ⁠were heard in the Ukrainian capital of ⁠Kyiv early ⁠on ​Tuesday, a Reuters witness said, as Russia ⁠continues its near-daily attacks. Missile ‌debris fell in the ‌courtyard of a residential building, among other damage, and a non-residential building caught fire in another ‌part of the city, Kyiv mayor ​Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram. On Monday, Zelenskyy said nine ⁠people had been killed and more ​than ​80 injured ​in Russian drone strikes ​throughout ‌the country, ​including ​in Kyiv. Pope Leo urged Russia and ⁠Ukraine to sit down and discuss how to end their war , hours after ⁠he had urged ⁠European leaders ​seeking to end conflicts to make concessions to achieve peace. Addressing a press conference aboard his ​flight to Rome on Monday after ‌a four-day trip ‌to France, Leo said the 1.4-billion-member Catholic church had an obligation ‌to call for peace and respect of human life. “The Church has a responsibility to promote these values, continually inviting leaders – from Russia and Ukraine, as well as other countries – to come together, sit down, engage ‌in dialogue,” the pope said. Nato’s top military commander said Russia’s sabotage campaign in Europe was failing to put countries off supporting Ukraine . “State-directed sabotage is growing increasingly brazen,” US general Alexus Grynkewich told a committee of EU lawmakers on Monday. Nato’s supreme allied commander for Europe cited recent incidents including the discovery of an explosive-laden drone at a German airport and a Russian naval ship firing flares at a Danish helicopter. “These are clear examples of attempts to instil fear and fracture our unified support to Ukraine. It isn’t working,” he said. Ukraine will postpone some spending commitments, including reconstruction work, because of delays in receiving aid from its foreign backers , Ukraine’s prime minister said. The government would carry out these projects eventually, “but for now, all resources must be directed toward critical areas”, Sergiy Koretsky said on Telegram on Monday. Russia’s offensive has battered Ukraine’s economy, causing billions of dollars in destruction and punching a huge hole in its neighbour’s finances. Putin has ordered the Russian assets of German retailer Metro AG to be placed under temporary administration , amid Russian-German tensions over the Ukraine war. The order, posted on Monday on the government website, did not state a reason. The step follows similar steps against the Russia businesses of global food company Nestlé and French retailer Auchan under a 2023 decree aimed at businesses associated with “unfriendly countries”. Temporary administration has led to local owners taking over the Russia businesses of French dairy concern Danone and Danish brewer Carlsberg at knockdown prices. A Russian jet-powered drone struck a Ukrainian village near the Polish border earlier on Monday, damaging a border checkpoint, a regional Ukrainian official said. The official did not give details about the nature of the checkpoint or extent of damage from the blast. Russia has launched multiple attacks near Ukraine’s border with Poland in recent weeks, drawing condemnation from Warsaw and its European allies. Continue reading...

data.title: La dette publique française s’envole à 119 % du PIB, du jamais-vu depuis 1946
data.description: L’endettement de la France s’établissait à 3 595,5 milliards d’euros à la fin de juin, a annoncé l’Insee, mardi 29 septembre. Rapporté à l’activité économique, il se situe à son plus haut niveau depuis 1946. Et ne peut que monter encore.

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : l’Estonie accuse la Russie d’avoir commis « un acte de sabotage » en incendiant les locaux d’un fabricant de drones
data.description: « Nous pouvons conclure avec certitude que l’attaque incendiaire contre les locaux de Milrem Robotics (…) a été un acte de sabotage commandité par les services spéciaux de la Fédération de Russie », a dit le ministre estonien des affaires étrangères, à propos de cet incident qui a eu lieu en août. data.title: Risk för mer oro när vardagens motgångar kallas trauma
data.description: Medicinska och psykiatriska termer har blivit en del av vardagsspråket. Krävande eller bara pinsamma händelser beskrivs ibland som rena trauman. data.title: De säljer sex – och sina ägg
data.description: Niklas Thenstedt har längtat efter egna barn i nästan 20 år. Nu har han ett avtal med en klinik i Colombia som garanterar att en surrugoatmamma ska föda hans barn. Han har träffat kvinnan som ska bära hans barn, men vem är kvinnan som har donerat sina ägg – den genetiska mamman? Det vet Niklas inte, identiteten är skyddad av sekretess. När DN och reportern Josefin Sköld börjar nysta i branschen så framträder ett mönster – kvinnor som är äggdonatorer är också verksamma i livesexindustrin.

data.title: Hvorfor holder fuglene sig væk? Uforklarlige fænomener har givet en lille norsk dal ufo-feber
data.description: Kim Nyland har set lysene med sine egne øjne. Og han har set en lilla kugle, der svævede over en sø. De uforklarlige fænomener sker flere gange om måneden i Hessdalen i Norge. Lys på nattehimlen, en mystisk jordbiopsi og et bestemt område, hvor fugle ikke flyver ind. Og så er der også Helge Otterå, der for syv år siden så to høje væsener med ovale hoveder komme løbende nede fra floden. Tag med til det gådefulde område, hvor mange er sikre på, at der er besøg fra andre civilisationer i universet.

data.title: 'Ik had een gigantisch bedrag aan een oplichter gegeven.' De prosecco-oogst in Italië leunt op migranten, maar onder Meloni zijn zij kwetsbaar voor uitbuiting

data.title: Poczta Polska wzmacnia infrastrukturę logistyczną i rozwija obsługę gotówki
data.description: Rozwijamy naszą infrastrukturę logistyczną, inwestujemy w sortery, testujemy różne pojazdy i chcemy wdrażać nową mobilność. Jednocześnie inwestujemy 270 mln zł w rozwój logistyki gotówki – to niezwykle ważny obszar wzmacniający odporność państwa w sytuacjach kryzysowych – mówi Sławomir Żurawski, wiceprezes ds. operacyjnych Poczty Polskiej. Jak Poczta rozumie nową mobilność i co robi, by ją wdrażać?

data.title: Polska motoryzacja po 1989 roku nie miała strategii. Compass 2035 wyznacza kierunek
data.description: Fabrykę można zbudować, ale klientów trzeba jeszcze przekonać. Maciej Mazur, prezes Polskiego Stowarzyszenia Nowej Mobilności, wyjaśnia, dlaczego polska motoryzacja potrzebuje stabilnych zasad zamiast dopłat z datą ważności. W rozmowie o strategii Compass 2035 mówi też o szansach na przełom w Jaworznie i o tym, co może skłonić kierowców do przesiadki do elektryka.

data.title: Návrh na nedůvěru vládě není divadlo, říká Kupka. Řečniště obsadí ministři
data.description: Na mimořádné schůzi Sněmovny se scházejí poslanci. data.title: Pohřešovaná matka měla psychické potíže, z domácnosti zmizely nože a světlo na kolo
data.description: Téměř měsíc po zmizení policie pohřešovanou osmatřicetiletou Janu Šerjeníkovou z Frýdku-Místku stále nenašla. Podle vedení krajské kriminálky na tom byla v poslední době psychicky špatně a snažila se najít odbornou pomoc. Policie má čtyři vyšetřovací verze, k žádné se zatím nepřiklání. Asistentka Krajského soudu v Ostravě a matka dvou dětí zmizela na začátku září.

data.title: Češi nevěří AI nástrojům, velká část z nich je vnímá jako hrozbu, říká průzkum
data.description: V Česku se za poslední dva roky prudce zvýšil počet lidí, kteří používají AI nástroje, momentálně jde už o 76 procent. Zároveň však 39 procent obyvatel říká, že má z rozvoje umělé inteligence obavy, pokles v důvěře je znatelný především u mladých lidí, kteří se obávají například deepfake obsahu. Vychází to z průzkumu Index inovací od společností ČSOB a Mastercard.

data.title: Estonsko obvinilo Rusko ze žhářského útoku na zbrojovku. Moskva vinu odmítá
data.description: Estonsko uvedlo, že dospělo k závěru, že srpnový požár v tallinském zbrojním podniku Milrem Robotics byl způsoben žhářským útokem provedeným na rozkaz ruských tajných služeb. data.title: Co jsme slíbili, jsme splnili, tvrdí primátor Jihlavy. Na Facebooku ale nereaguje
data.description: O hlasy v komunálních volbách v krajském městě Vysočiny bude letos usilovat uskupení s nevšedním názvem. Tým pro Jihlavu. Síly v něm spojily ODS, KDU-ČSL a TOP 09. data.title: Fanoušci Slipknot hrozí kapele bojkotem kvůli účasti Marilyna Mansona na turné
data.description: Heavymetalová kapela Slipknot oznámila k radosti svých fanoušků velkolepé turné, se kterým projede především oba americké kontinenty. data.title: OBRAZEM: Bangkok zaplavila voda. Děti plavou ulicemi, školy zůstávají zavřené
data.description: Povodně v Bangkoku zasáhly zhruba 700 000 lidí. Od vyhlášení stavu ohrožení uplynuly tři dny a část thajské metropole stále zůstává pod vodou. Školy jsou už druhý den zavřené. data.title: Přívoz přes Lipno kvůli nedostatku vody přerušil provoz, poprvé po 23 letech
data.description: Kvůli nedostatku vody v lipenské přehradě ukončil provoz přívoz mezi Horní Planou a Bližší Lhotou. Denně přepravil přibližně stovku aut, která nyní musejí nádrž objíždět. data.title: Korunovační klenoty se vrátily do katedrály, letos přilákaly desetitisíce lidí
data.description: Sedm klíčníků dnes uložilo korunovační klenoty zpět do Korunní komory ve svatovítské katedrále na Pražském hradě. Lidé si klenoty mohli prohlédnout od 15. do 28. září, první čtyři dny byly vyhrazeny školákům. České korunovační klenoty vidělo ve Vladislavském sále Pražského hradu za 14 dní zhruba 36 600 lidí. Z toho asi 9000 bylo žáků škol.

data.title: Noční požár ubytovny v Trutnově. Dvěma lidem plameny odřízly cestu ven
data.description: V Trutnově v pondělí večer vyhořela ubytovna. Když hasiči dorazili k dvoupodlažní budově na Středním Předměstí, z okna jednoho z pokojů v patře už šlehaly plameny. Po nastavovacím žebříku hasiči zachránili dva lidi, kteří nestihli před ohněm utéct . Příčinou požáru se zabývá vyšetřovatel, škoda je předběžně tři miliony korun.

data.title: Nova se podělí o práva na NHL s Primou. Fanoušci uvidí až 24 zápasů týdně
data.description: Hokejoví fanoušci se mohou v sezoně 2026/27 těšit na širší nabídku přenosů NHL. Nova a Prima totiž přinesou v základní části až 24 utkání týdně. Každý z vysílatelů bude mít k dispozici 14 zápasů, z toho deset exkluzivně a čtyři dostupné oběma televizním skupinám. Spolupráce vychází z nové dohody, že Nova poskytne Primě část televizních práv na NHL. Vybraná utkání budou dostupná také ve volném vysílání.

data.title: Imunita Čechů? Orchestr, který se nedá naladit jedním tlačítkem, říkají experti
data.description: O imunitu se podle průzkumů zajímá většina Čechů, skutečně se o ni ale stará jen menší část z nich. Odborníci přitom varují před představou, že obranyschopnost lze jednoduše „nakopnout“ vitaminy či doplňky stravy. Co je klíčem, o tom v pořadu iDNES Lounge diskutovali Markéta Bloomfield, primářka Ústavu imunologie 2. LF UK a FN Motol a Homolka, Jana Vydláková, vedoucí Ambulance klinické imunologie a alergologie IKEM a Jan Řepa ze společnosti NaturaMed.

data.title: Chybějí mi blízcí a běžné okamžiky, říká o svém úspěchu německý DJ Boris Brejcha
data.description: Ve světě elektronické taneční hudby (EDM) patří německý DJ Boris Brejcha již dvě desetiletí k etablovaným hudebním producentům. Maskovaný hudebník a autor hitů jako Gravity nebo Purple Noise proslul díky stylu high-tech minimal, který sám vytvořil a zpopularizoval. Svou tvorbu předvede fanouškům na české půdě, kam se rád vrací, již v pátek 2. října v pražské O2 areně. Před blížícím se koncertem poskytl redakci iDNES.cz exkluzivní rozhovor.

data.title: Další problém Dědkova hnutí. Kandidát použil v kampani maily pacientů
data.description: Nové politické hnutí miliardáře Petra Dědka Srdcem pro Pardubice má další problém, poté co využilo sportovní klub k agitaci. Předseda hnutí a čtyřka na kandidátce do voleb, praktický lékař pro dospělé a emeritní primář ARO Vítězslav Novohradský, rozeslal svým pacientům e-mail s pozvánkou na politický mítink. Lidé mu přitom kontakty poskytli s tím, aby s nimi komunikoval o jejich zdravotním stavu. Zda lékař zneužil databázi pacientů, bude zkoumat Úřad na ochranu osobních údajů. Lékař na konkrétní otázky odpovědět odmítl.

data.title: Portugal tem das classes docentes mais envelhecidas da OCDE
data.description: Portugal é dos países onde o corpo docente está mais envelhecido, com uma elevada percentagem de professores com mais de 55 anos, e a profissão tende a ser menos atrativa e pouco reconhecida pela sociedade. Os dados são de um novo relatório da Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Económico (OCDE), que indica que quanto aos estudantes, há progressos na escolarização, mas há ainda 36 por cento da população portuguesa que não completou o ensino secundário.

data.title: Elecciones 2026: ¿Hay segunda vuelta para alcaldes provinciales y distritales? Esto establece la ley
data.description: Este 4 de octubre, los electores elegirán a sus alcaldes provinciales y distritales en una sola jornada. A diferencia de la elección de gobernador regional, para las alcaldías no existe segunda vuelta ni se exige un porcentaje mínimo de votos para ganar. En elecciones anteriores, algunas incluso se definieron por un estrecho margen de votos o, en casos de empate, mediante un sorteo.

data.title: Pension de vieillesse, une réforme à deux vitesses
data.description: La revalorisation des pensions de retraite entrée en vigueur en août 2026 fait des heureux mais aussi des mécontents. Les retraités concernés par la mesure voient désormais leur pension de vieillesse portée jusqu’à 60 % de leur dernier salaire net. Une avancée qui ne profite toutefois pas à tous.  Pour l’économiste Jean Ndenzako, cette mesure améliore le niveau de vie des retraités concernés mais creuse l’écart avec les assurés du privé et du parapublic.

data.title: Sangwa Patrick et le serment d’Intwari : « Tout reste possible »
data.description:
L'homme qui refuse de ployer. 
 Bujumbura retient son souffle. 
 À la veille d'une bataille annoncée comme funeste et à l'heure où les esprits chagrins enterraient déjà les Intamba après la déconvenue face au Togo, un homme s'est levé.  Droit et impavide, il avait à sa droite l'emblématique capitaine Yussuf Ndayishimiye. Et à sa gauche le brillantissime Secrétaire Général Adjoint de la FFB en la personne de Melchiade Nkeshimana, jouant le rôle de modérateur. 
 Ce lundi 28 septembre 2026, dans une des salles sublimes du Stade Intwari, le sélectionneur Patrick Sangwa n'a pas convoqué la presse pour s'excuser. Il l'a convoquée pour raviver la flamme.

data.title: Agathon Rwasa réfute un arrêt aux motifs jugés erronés
data.description: L’opposant politique Agathon Rwasa et son équipe déclarent que la Chambre administrative de la Cour suprême vient de se dérober et refuser « délibérément » de connaître leur requête au détriment des considérations étrangères au corps du dossier. L’arrêt RAP 68 rendu par la Cour le 07 août leur a été signifié le 21 septembre 2026. Agathon Rwasa affirme qu’il y a un agenda caché de l’écarter de la course présidentielle prochaine, mais déclare qu’il va participer. Interview.

data.title: FNL soutient Ndayishimiye et demande une amnistie pour les prisonniers politiques
data.description: Le parti Forces nationales de libération (FNL) demande au président de la République, Évariste Ndayishimiye, d’accorder une amnistie aux personnes qu’il considère comme des prisonniers politiques et de lever les mandats d’arrêt visant d’autres personnes. Cette demande a été formulée dimanche 27 septembre par Jacques Bigirimana, président du FNL, à l’issue du congrès national du parti consacré notamment à la position de la formation politique pour l’élection présidentielle de 2027. Par Jules Bercy Igiraneza

data.title: BEAC : statu quo monétaire malgré le ralentissement de la croissance en zone CEMAC
data.description: © DR Réuni le 28 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé sous la présidence d'Yvon Sana Bangui, le Comité de Politique Monétaire de la BEAC a maintenu ses taux directeurs inchangés : TIAO à 4,50%, facilité de prêt marginal à 5,75%, facilité de dépôt à 0,00% et réserves obligatoires à 6,50% à vue et 4,00% à terme. Prudence et stabilité pour la CEMAC. Le Comité de Politique Monétaire (CPM) de la Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC) a tenu sa troisième session ordinaire de l'année, le lundi 28 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé, sous la présidence de Monsieur Yvon SANA BANGUI, Gouverneur de la BEAC. Au cours de cette session, le CPM a examiné les perspectives macroéconomiques internationales et sous-régionales, ainsi que la situation du système financier de la CEMAC. Au niveau international, le FMI prévoit, selon sa mise à jour de juillet 2026, une croissance mondiale qui reviendrait à 3,0% en 2026 contre 3,5% en 2025, en raison des tensions géopolitiques. Au niveau de la CEMAC, les prévisions de la BEAC tablent sur un ralentissement : croissance à 3,0% contre 3,7% en 2025, inflation contenue sous la norme communautaire à 2,2% contre 2,0%, repli du déficit budgétaire hors dons de 4,5% à 3,3% du PIB, et amélioration du déficit courant à 2,8% contre 4,2%. La masse monétaire progresserait de 10,6%, les réserves de change passeraient à 4,53 mois d'importations contre 4,07 mois, et le taux de couverture extérieure s'établirait à 72,4% contre 65,2% en 2025. En définitive, le CPM a décidé le statu quo monétaire pour accompagner la résilience tout en préservant la stabilité. Cet article BEAC : statu quo monétaire malgré le ralentissement de la croissance en zone CEMAC est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun-MRC : pourquoi ‘’l’autorisation’’ du 28 septembre change tout après Kamto et Mota
data.description: © MRC L'obtention du récépissé N°000332 pour la convention du 17 octobre n'est pas une simple formalité administrative. C'est la première victoire politique de l'après-Kamto, et elle dit beaucoup sur la stratégie de survie du MRC. Pendant 10 mois, le MRC vivait dans une fiction juridique. Le ministre de l’Administration territoriale -Minat, le 19 août dernier, avait été clair. Il ne reconnaît plus rien depuis la 3ème convention ordinaire des 9 et 10 décembre 2023. Tout ce qui a été fait après - y compris la visioconférence du 21 décembre 2025 qui avait reconduit Maurice Kamto - est frappé de nullité à ses yeux. Par conséquent, le parti était comme sans direction légalement reconnue, puis décapité par deux démissions coup sur coup, celle du président Maurice Kamto et celle de son numéro 1 historique Mamadou Mota. Dans ce vide, qui pouvait parler au nom du MRC ? Le Minat a répondu indirectement ce 28 septembre : il faut choisir la personne. Mais avant, la démarche suivie pour obtenir le récépissé n’est pas anodine. Le choix de l'homme qui dépose la demande est un message juridique Ce n'est pas Tiriane Balbine Noah la présidente par intérim qui dépose. C'est Justin Roger Noah, Secrétaire Général Adjoint n°1. Il est issu de la dernière direction reconnue par le Minat, celle de décembre 2023. En acceptant son dossier, le sous-préfet de Yaoundé IV, et à travers lui le Minat qui publie le récépissé sur sa page, reconnaît de facto qu'il est un interlocuteur légitime. C'est une rupture avec novembre 2025, où ce même arrondissement avait interdit la convention de Kamto. Cette fois, l'administration dit oui. Cela signifie qu'elle considère que la démarche de l'équipe intérimaire rentre dans la légalité de 2023, pas dans l'illégalité de 2025. Pour Tiriane Noah, présidente par intérim, c'est une légitimation par procuration. Elle ne pouvait pas déposer elle-même sans que le Minat ne conteste sa qualité. Elle passe par le SGA1, qui lui, est inattaquable sur le plan administratif. Fin de la stratégie de la chaise vide Après les démissions, deux options s'offraient au MRC. La première était le pourrissement. Rester dans la contestation de la décision du 19 août, crier à l'acharnement, et ne pas tenir de convention. La deuxième était le réalisme. Revenir à la case départ légale de 2023, et refaire tout le processus dans les règles exigées par le Minat pour exister à nouveau. Tiriane Noah et ceux qui l’entourent ont choisi l'option 2. Sa tournée à Ngaoundéré et Garoua ce week-end, l'installation d'un bureau régional, la présentation d'une liste pour le 17 octobre, et maintenant ce récépissé, sont les étapes d'une même stratégie qui vise à reconstruire la légalité par le bas. Le soutien de Mamadou Mota, devenu coordonnateur de sa campagne, est essentiel dans ce schéma. Mota était l'autre démissionnaire. En revenant comme parrain, il colmate la fracture morale laissée par les départs et évite que le MRC ne soit perçu comme un parti abandonné par ses chefs. Le vrai test de la convention du 17 octobre Avoir ‘’l'autorisation’’ de tenir la convention est une chose. Faire reconnaître son procès-verbal par le Minat en est une autre. C'est là que tout s'est bloqué en décembre 2025. Le parti avait tenu sa convention malgré l'interdiction, et le Minat avait refusé de reconnaître les résolutions. data.translatedDescription: © MRC L'obtention du récépissé N°000332 pour la convention du 17 octobre n'est pas une simple formalité administrative. C'est la première victoire politique de l'après-Kamto, et elle dit beaucoup sur la stratégie de survie du MRC. Pendant 10 mois, le MRC vivait dans une fiction juridique. Le ministre de l’Administration territoriale -Minat, le 19 août dernier, avait été clair. Il ne reconnaît plus rien depuis la 3ème convention ordinaire des 9 et 10 décembre 2023. Tout ce qui a été fait après - y compris la visioconférence du 21 décembre 2025 qui avait reconduit Maurice Kamto - est frappé de nullité à ses yeux. Par conséquent, le parti était comme sans direction légalement reconnue, puis décapité par deux démissions coup sur coup, celle du président Maurice Kamto et celle de son numéro 1 historique Mamadou Mota. Dans ce vide, qui pouvait parler au nom du MRC ? Le Minat a répondu indirectement ce 28 septembre : il faut choisir la personne. Mais avant, la démarche suivie pour obtenir le récépissé n’est pas anodine. Le choix de l'homme qui dépose la demande est un message juridique Ce n'est pas Tiriane Balbine Noah la présidente par intérim qui dépose. C'est Justin Roger Noah, Secrétaire Général Adjoint n°1. data.title: Cameroun/ Maurice Kamto dénonce les universitaires : le réquisitoire d’un initié contre le « blanchiment juridique » des dictatures
data.description: © DR Quand Maurice Kamto lance : « Ils sont allés chercher la lumière, parfois jusqu'à l'étranger, pour venir plonger leurs pays dans les ténèbres », il ne s'adresse pas aux militants. Il s'adresse à ses pairs. À ses confrères des amphis de Yaoundé, Dakar, Abidjan. Ce n'est pas l'opposant qui parle. C'est le professeur. L'ancien Doyen de la Faculté des sciences juridiques et politiques de l’université de Yaoundé II connaît la mécanique de l'intérieur. Et c'est précisément ce qui rend sa charge aussi violente. Dans sa pensée du 28 septembre 2026, l’universitaire fait remarquer que le coup d'Etat ne porte plus de treillis, il porte une toge. Pour Kamto, l'Afrique francophone a connu une mutation du coup d'Etat. Le plus fréquent n'est plus celui du colonel qui prend la radio. C'est celui du professeur agrégé qui prend la Constitution. « Au total, il y a eu dans nos pays plus de coups d'Etat constitutionnels que de coups d'Etat militaires au cours des quatre dernières décennies. » Sa thèse est celle du blanchiment juridique : le dirigeant véreux ne veut plus violer la Loi fondamentale les armes à la main. Il veut qu'un constitutionnaliste respecté vienne expliquer, avec un vernis scientifique, que la violation est en réalité légale. Comment on fabrique un 3e mandat proprement Kamto décrit en trois pièces la recette, qu'il a vue à l'œuvre. D’abord, elle consiste à supprimer la limitation de mandats, acquise dans l'euphorie démocratique des années 1990. Ensuite, au lieu de demander au peuple souverain par référendum, on fait voter la suppression par un parlement acquis. Enfin, on justifie l'opération par une aberration juridique pour un républicain : la souveraineté du président serait supérieure à celle du Peuple. « Ils défendent sans vergogne sa violation, les changements constitutionnels fondamentaux par de simples révisions parlementaires, sans recours au référendum ». Pour le juriste qu'est Maurice Kamto, c'est une trahison du principe premier de la République. Le Peuple est la source de toute souveraineté. Aucune autre ne peut lui être supérieure. Une accusation de complicité historique La phrase finale est la plus lourde : « Assurément, nombre d'universitaires africains ne sont pas moins comptables de nos malheurs que les gouvernants. » Il ne dit pas qu'ils sont des victimes ou des conseillers mal écoutés. Il dit qu'ils sont comptables. Co-responsables. En creux, Kamto pose la question qui fâche dans toutes les facultés de droit du continent : à quoi sert d'aller chercher la lumière de la science si c'est pour l'éteindre à son retour ? Comme un universitaire dans un amphithéâtre, entouré de garanties d’indépendance, d’impartialité, d’objectivité reconnues à la science, l’enseignant et homme politique se rapproche de Mamadi Doumbouya, président guinéen. Du haut de la Tribune des Nations Unies lors de l’Assemblée générale de septembre 2026, celui qui est arrivé au pouvoir par coup d’Etat en 2021 puis maintenu après élection en 2025, dénonce l’impunité des ‘’putschistes en costume’’. Ces dirigeants qui modifient la Constitution pour se maintenir au pouvoir en toute impunité. Ces derniers se font ainsi aider par d’éminents universitaires tel qu’indique le Pr Maurice Kamto, lui qui a fait ses pas aux cotés du régime de Yaoundé avant de prendre ses distances. Cet article Cameroun/ Maurice Kamto dénonce les universitaires : le réquisitoire d’un initié contre le « blanchiment juridique » des dictatures est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Quinze ans après, le port de Kribi construit par une entreprise chinoise stimule la croissance du Cameroun et améliore les conditions de vie (REPORTAGE)
data.description: © Xinhua Il y a quinze ans, Mboro, à la périphérie de Kribi, ville dans le sud du Cameroun , n'était qu'un petit village de pêcheurs isolé, avec quelques maisons reliées par d'étroites pistes sinueuses en terre. Aujourd'hui, cette même portion du littoral abrite l'un des ports en eau profonde les plus modernes d'Afrique centrale, tandis que les environs se transforment sous l'impulsion d'une économie industrielle et logistique en plein essor. Depuis les années 1970, le Cameroun envisageait la construction d'un port en eau profonde pour compléter le port de Douala, principal port du pays, situé dans un estuaire peu profond ne permettant pas d'accueillir de grands navires. Ce projet envisagé depuis plusieurs décennies s'est concrétisé avec l'achèvement des première et deuxième phases du port en eau profonde de Kribi. UNE VILLE TOURNEE VERS L'AVENIR Gu Gaobai faisait partie des premiers Chinois arrivés en 2011 avec la China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC), entreprise chargée de la construction du port en eau profonde de Kribi. "Lorsque nous nous sommes dirigés vers le site du projet, nous avancions péniblement sur d'étroites pistes en terre. A l'endroit choisi, nous ne voyions qu'une petite plage de sable et quelques récifs. A l'époque, ces récifs étaient les seuls repères permettant de situer l'emplacement du futur port", se souvenait Gu Gaobai, aujourd'hui directeur général des projets de la CHEC au Cameroun. La transformation est visible le long des routes menant au port. Une piste étroite a laissé place à une route à chaussées séparées, avec un passage pour piétons au milieu. De nouveaux bâtiments, commerces et équipements publics sont apparus avec l'essor de l'activité économique. Pour Jean-Kalvin Assembe, habitant local de 50 ans, ces changements se ressentent jusque dans la vie quotidienne. "Je suis heureux et épanoui dans cette ville", a-t-il déclaré. L'arrivée de travailleurs et d'entreprises a créé davantage de possibilités pour les habitants et contribué à soutenir les revenus des ménages. "Même les petits commerces de quartier ont désormais des clients. Cela apporte vraiment des changements positifs", a-t-il souligné. Des immeubles, des hôpitaux, des universités et des centres commerciaux jalonnent désormais Kribi. Des lampadaires éclairent les routes autrefois plongées dans l'obscurité, tandis que la zone portuaire reste fortement éclairée après la tombée de la nuit. Les chauffeurs de poids lourds comptent également parmi les bénéficiaires du développement du port. De longues files de camions se forment quotidiennement dans la zone portuaire. "Le port nous a donné l'occasion de découvrir la région", a raconté Yaya Aboubakar, 68 ans, chauffeur chevronné ayant sillonné quatre pays d'Afrique centrale. "Kribi nous a facilité les choses. Le service est également rapide". "Beaucoup de clients et d'experts qui connaissent la Chine disent souvent que Kribi est le Shenzhen du Cameroun , une 'ville du futur'", a affirmé Gu Gaobai. UN POLE D'INDUSTRIALISATION ET D'INTEGRATION REGIONALE A mesure que le port s'est développé, sa zone industrielle s'est étendue. Patrick Mpila Ayissi, responsable des infrastructures de la Zone industrielle du port de Kribi, a indiqué que les investissements dans cette zone se sont accélérés depuis le début de ses activités en 2018. "Depuis 2018, les opérateurs industriels ont investi près de 400 milliards de francs CFA (environ 700 millions de dollars), et 93 autorisations d'occupation ont été délivrées, tandis que 18 entreprises sont déjà opérationnelles", a-t-il précisé. L'ambition est passée d'une zone logistique initiale de 455 hectares à une zone industrielle intégrée de 4.000 hectares, a-t-il ajouté. Selon M. Ayissi, la zone devrait attirer près de 900 millions de dollars d'investissements et créer 50.000 emplois directs, avec jusqu'à 150.000 emplois directs et indirects au total au cours des 15 prochaines années. Le port est également devenu une plateforme stratégique pour l'Afrique centrale, desservant les marchés des pays voisins. "Le trafic de conteneurs a quadruplé depuis 2018, dépassant 555.000 EVP en 2025, tandis que le volume global des marchandises a dépassé 12,7 millions de tonnes en 2024", a indiqué M. Ayissi. Les échanges commerciaux transitent déjà de Kribi vers le Gabon, la République centrafricaine, le Tchad, le Congo et la Guinée équatoriale, a-t-il précisé, ajoutant que les connexions régionales du port ont été renforcées par des compagnies maritimes telles que MSC. Pour accompagner l'essor du réseau logistique, la CHEC a également construit la route Kribi-Lolabé. "Cette route relie le port en eau profonde de Kribi aux principales villes du pays, facilitant les déplacements des personnes et le transport des marchandises, et contribuant ainsi à l'industrialisation du Cameroun ", a expliqué Emmanuel Nganou Djoumessi, ministre cameroun ais des Travaux publics. DES COMPETENCES QUI CHANGENT DES VIES Les transformations liées au port se reflètent également dans les parcours professionnels des travailleurs locaux. En 2013, Ngatugirius Ndenya a quitté son emploi de soudeur à Yaoundé pour rejoindre la CHEC à Kribi. "Lorsque je suis arrivé ici en 2013, les débuts ont été très difficiles pour moi", a raconté cet homme de 53 ans. La CHEC a adopté une méthode consistant à associer des travailleurs cameroun ais à des collègues chinois expérimentés, leur permettant d'acquérir une expérience pratique avant d'assumer eux-mêmes certaines tâches. "Avant de venir ici, j'étais simplement soudeur sur plateforme. Mais maintenant, je peux tout faire dans le domaine de la soudure", a expliqué M. Ndenya. "Les jeunes qui sont arrivés ici n'étaient pas des techniciens, mais aujourd'hui, ils le sont". Pour certains travailleurs, le port transformé les conditions de vie. "Lorsque je suis arrivé ici, je n'avais absolument rien. J'avais quitté un emploi où je gagnais peut-être 100.000 francs CFA par mois", a raconté Armand Guehoada, aujourd'hui chargé des affaires commerciales à la CHEC. "Au bout d'un certain temps, j'ai pu acheter un véhicule. Aujourd'hui, j'en suis à mon troisième. Je peux facilement subvenir aux besoins de ma famille", a-t-il ajouté. "Au cours des 15 dernières années, nous avons formé un grand nombre de professionnels locaux dans les domaines de la construction portuaire et de l'ingénierie des grands projets. Beaucoup de ceux qui ont travaillé sur le port contribuent aujourd'hui au développement de la zone industrielle voisine", a souligné Gu Gaobai. Cette année marque le 55e anniversaire de l'établissement des relations diplomatiques entre la Chine et le Cameroun , tandis que le port en eau profonde de Kribi célèbre les 15 ans du début de sa construction. "Kribi reste un symbole visible de la coopération entre le Cameroun et la Chine. Son développement repose depuis le départ sur des financements concessionnels accordés par des institutions chinoises, ce qui témoigne d'un partenariat véritablement inscrit dans la durée", a estimé Patrick Mpila Ayissi. Pour Patrice Melom, directeur général de l'Autorité portuaire de Kribi, le développement du port a ouvert de nouvelles perspectives pour la ville et le pays. "L'avenir du port de Kribi est prometteur, avec des résultats concrets et des perspectives extrêmement positives. Il nous appartient désormais de mobiliser toutes nos énergies pour faire de cette infrastructure un véritable moteur d'une croissance durable, au service de la prospérité nationale et de l'intégration sous-régionale", a-t-il affirmé. Xinhua Cet article Quinze ans après, le port de Kribi construit par une entreprise chinoise stimule la croissance du Cameroun et améliore les conditions de vie (REPORTAGE) est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
